newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Daschle calls for quick action on Pena.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Daschle calls for quick action on Pena.

text.p: U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle Thursday urged quick Senate confirmation of Federico Pena as energy secretary, after the Senate Energy Committee postponed its approval vote on Pena.

"Federico Pena conducted himself very well during his hearing earlier this year. He answered satisfactorily all the questions that were put to him and showed that he is ready to lead the Department of Energy," Daschle said in a statement.
The Senate Energy Committee had been slated to vote on Pena's nomination February 12, but then rescheduled the vote tentatively for February 26.
"The committee is not finished looking into all the details surrounding his nomination," a committee spokesman said.

A White House official earlier this week said it appeared Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, was holding up Pena's confirmation to try to get the administration to agree to a plan for interim storage of waste from commercial nuclear power plants.
However, the committee spokesman has maintained that nuclear waste storage and Pena's confirmation are separate issues.
Daschle in his statement said he expected Pena to be confirmed by the full Senate quickly after the committee action.
"The Department of Energy serves critical functions, and its top leadership position should not go unfilled a day longer than is necessary," Daschle said.
